title: Fair value measurements — Prairie Grain Cooperative
instructions: Prairie Grain Cooperative reports several items at fair value at December 31. Determine the fair value hierarchy levels and compute the fair value of its wheat inventory held for trading.

exhibits.title: Items measured at fair value
exhibits.content:
1. **Listed equity securities** — valued at NYSE closing prices.
2. **Interest rate swap** — valued with a model using observable LIBOR-replacement (SOFR) forward curves.
3. **Investment in a private agritech startup** — valued with a DCF using management's revenue projections and a discount rate derived from internal estimates.
4. **Corporate bonds** — valued using quoted prices for similar bonds, as the specific bonds trade infrequently.

exhibits.title: Wheat inventory (100,000 bushels)
exhibits.content:
| Market | Price per bushel | Transaction cost per bushel | Transport cost per bushel | Share of Prairie's historical volume |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Chicago exchange | 6.20 | 0.30 | 0.40 | 85% |
| Local elevator | 6.00 | 0.05 | 0.10 | 15% |

parts.prompt: Select the fair value hierarchy level for each item.

rows.label: 1. Listed equity securities
rows.explanation: Quoted prices, identical assets, active market.

rows.label: 4. Corporate bonds
rows.explanation: Quoted prices for similar items / inactive markets.

rows.label: Fair value per bushel
rows.explanation: Chicago is the principal market (greatest volume). Fair value = 6.20 − 0.40 transport = **5.80**. Transaction costs aren't deducted — and the local elevator's higher net (5.85) is irrelevant when a principal market exists.

rows.label: Total fair value of the wheat

parts.prompt: Which excerpt (paraphrased for study) explains why the Chicago exchange price is used even though the local elevator would net more per bushel?

excerpts.text: A fair value measurement assumes the transaction takes place in the principal market for the asset or, in the absence of a principal market, in the most advantageous market.

The price in the principal (or most advantageous) market is not adjusted for transaction costs, but is adjusted for costs to transport the asset to that market if location is a characteristic of the asset.
Inputs are categorized into three levels, giving the highest priority to quoted prices in active markets for identical assets.
The fair value option may be elected on an instrument-by-instrument basis and is irrevocable.

parts.explanation: When a principal market exists, it is used even if another market offers a better net price at the measurement date. (Excerpt b explains the cost adjustments, not the market choice.)
